Describe a cohort flow in words, for a methods section

Source: R/narrative.R
as_narrative.Rd

Writes the attrition cascade as a short paragraph, ready to paste into the participant-flow part of a methods or results section. The numbers come from as_attrition_tibble() (and, after a randomise() step, from the same per-arm re-application as_consort_diagram() uses), so the text always agrees with the table and the diagram.

Usage

as_narrative(
  flow,
  assessed_label = "assessed for eligibility",
  unit = "participants",
  count_by = NULL,
  big_mark = ",",
  digits = 1L,
  show_categories = TRUE,
  drop_randomise = FALSE,
  lowercase_reasons = TRUE,
  style = c("prose", "bullets")
)

# S3 method for class 'cf_narrative'
print(x, ...)

Arguments

flow

A cf_flow object produced by apply_criteria().

assessed_label

Text after the starting count in the first sentence, as in "Of 200 participants assessed for eligibility". Default "assessed for eligibility".

unit

Plural noun for what is counted, used verbatim (it is not pluralised or inflected). Default "participants".

count_by

Optional hierarchy level to count instead of rows, passed to as_attrition_tibble() (see there). Set unit to match.

big_mark

Thousands separator for counts ("1,234" with the default ","); "" turns grouping off.

digits

Decimal places for percentages. Default 1.

show_categories

Logical. When TRUE (default) steps with the same category are collapsed under a single parent row. When FALSE one row per step is produced.

drop_randomise

Logical. When TRUE, a randomise() step is ignored and everything is reported pooled, as if there were no arms. Default FALSE.

lowercase_reasons

Logical. When TRUE (default), the first letter of each reason is lower-cased so it reads mid-sentence ("Age missing" becomes "age missing"), unless the first word looks like an acronym (its second letter is upper case, as in "BMI missing"). Quoted labels (not meeting "<label>") are never changed.

style

"prose" (default) for one paragraph, or "bullets" for one sentence per line, each starting "- " (Markdown list items).

x

A cf_narrative object.

...

Ignored.

Value

A single string with class c("cf_narrative", "character"). Printing wraps it to the console width; in an R Markdown or Quarto chunk it is inserted as text. Use as.character() for the bare string.

Wording

  • One sentence per category (or per step with show_categories = FALSE, and for uncategorised steps). Category names group reasons into a sentence but are not themselves narrated. Steps and categories that removed nobody are left out.

  • The first sentence opens "Of N <assessed_label>, ..."; later ones open "A further ...". Each gives the number removed and its percentage of those entering that category or step, then the reason(s): one reason in brackets, several as a list with their own counts. The last sentence before randomisation (or before the final sentence) ends ", leaving n".

  • The removal text for each step is its reason. Exclusion steps default to their label; an inclusion step without a reason reads not meeting "<label>".

  • A randomise() step gives "The remaining n were randomised to A (n = a) and B (n = b)." Arms are in factor-level order (else sorted); a missing arm value forms an arm called "Missing", as in the diagram. After it, each sentence gives per-arm counts, with percentages of the number of that arm entering the step.

  • The last sentence gives the final cohort and its percentage of those assessed, broken down by arm when there are arms.

  • count_by changes what is counted but not the noun: set unit to match (e.g. count_by = "participant_id", unit = "participants" for a crossover trial with one row per participant-period).

  • Grouped steps read like any other step; units removed only because their group was removed (n_consequential) are not narrated separately.

Lists use the serial (Oxford) comma: "a, b, and c". The text is a starting point: read it, and edit it to suit the journal's style.

See also

as_attrition_tibble() and as_consort_diagram(), which report the same numbers.

Other reporting: as_attrition_table(), as_attrition_tibble(), as_characteristics_table(), as_characteristics_tibble(), as_consort_diagram(), save_consort_diagram()

Examples

dat  <- mock_parallel_rct(n_participants = 200, seed = 1)
crit <- cf_criteria() |>
  include(~ !is.na(age), label = "Age recorded", reason = "Age missing", category = "Age") |>
  include(~ age >= 18, label = "Aged 18 or over", reason = "Under 18", category = "Age") |>
  include(~ !is.na(consent_date), label = "Consented", reason = "Did not consent") |>
  randomise(by = "participant_id", arms = "arm") |>
  exclude(~ withdrew, label = "Withdrew consent")
flow <- apply_criteria(dat, crit, id = "participant_id")
as_narrative(flow)
#> Of 200 participants assessed for eligibility, 16 (8.0%) were excluded: age
#> missing (n = 10) and under 18 (n = 6). A further 41 (22.3%) were excluded (did
#> not consent), leaving 143. The remaining 143 were randomised to Control (n =
#> 74) and Intervention (n = 69). After randomisation, 3 (4.1%) in Control and 4
#> (5.8%) in Intervention were excluded (withdrew consent). The final cohort
#> comprised 136 participants (68.0% of those assessed): 71 in Control and 65 in
#> Intervention.
as_narrative(flow, style = "bullets")
#> - Of 200 participants assessed for eligibility, 16 (8.0%) were excluded: age
#>   missing (n = 10) and under 18 (n = 6).
#> - A further 41 (22.3%) were excluded (did not consent), leaving 143.
#> - The remaining 143 were randomised to Control (n = 74) and Intervention (n =
#>   69).
#> - After randomisation, 3 (4.1%) in Control and 4 (5.8%) in Intervention were
#>   excluded (withdrew consent).
#> - The final cohort comprised 136 participants (68.0% of those assessed): 71 in
#>   Control and 65 in Intervention.
as_narrative(flow, drop_randomise = TRUE)
#> Of 200 participants assessed for eligibility, 16 (8.0%) were excluded: age
#> missing (n = 10) and under 18 (n = 6). A further 41 (22.3%) were excluded (did
#> not consent). A further 7 (4.9%) were excluded (withdrew consent), leaving 136.
#> The final cohort comprised 136 participants (68.0% of those assessed).
